verdict.why: Option X provides superior measurability, cleaner contracts, and zero-context buildability without relying on unstated external context or contradicting the brief. Under the evidence and measurability lens: (1) Traceability & Fidelity: Option X enforces structured JSON meanings (`meanings-<N>.json`, C3) and mechanical inline tagging (`[M<n>]`) on every `REQ-*` and `Decisions` row (Design 3, REQ-3), whereas Option Y only checks Markdown heading order and `D<n>` set equality (C2, C3), leaving requirement coverage unmeasured. (2) Strict Adherence to Brief Facts: The brief explicitly demands 'one request each' for validators. Option X enforces zero retries (REQ-4, Design 4). Option Y invents a transport retry rule (C4, D9) and admits in R7 that a dropped connection causes a panelist to be 'called twice', violating the brief's constraint. Furthermore, the owner's order says 'without stinting' on Fable, while Option Y invents rigid state-based refusal rules (C4, D6) that block the thinker if an output section already has text. (3) Self-Containment vs. Unverifiable Sources: Option Y was generated via an external meanings file (`Meanings-sha256: 88f6...`) and cites it as a source in Q1-Q3 and Q18 without including it in the spec; C3 also leaves the required `Meanings:` header line out of its own code block (`Size: M` only), referring to Q22. Option Y's R15 requires replaying two finished M specs, yet Q23 admits 'no Size: M spec exists in this repository at 26bb446', making R15 unmeasurable at build time. Option X's quality measurement (Rollout step 6, REQ-14) is a forward-looking canary on the next three M/L specs with explicit metrics (round-1 accepted blocker/major findings, rounds to pass, fidelity findings). (4) Cost & Spend Accounting: Option X's cost rule (Design 5) explicitly checks `usage.is_byok` before falling back to heuristic comparisons, avoiding the double-counting risk Option Y admits in its Risks section ('OpenRouter may report u on ordinary calls with c below u; D15 would then double count'). Option X also records failed/timeout HTTP calls in the ledger (C5) and prevents projection volatility early in the month by waiting until day 7 (Design 6).
risks: Option X's inline `[M<n>]` tagging (Design 3) requires strict compliance from the subscription writer agent; if the writer omits tags or misformats tables, `spec_protocol.py check` will fail and require writer reruns.

Option X's `estate_cmd` parsing (Design 6) assumes one of three JSON shapes from Observatory (`totalUsd` at top-level, top-level array, or under `projects`); if Observatory outputs another shape, the ceiling check degrades to `local-only` until Rollout step 2's fixture is captured.

Option X passes `--meanings` only to the judge and keeps the panel blind (Design 4); if the writer subtly alters a meaning, only the judge catches it directly, whereas panelists only see the resulting spec text.
